ImageDescription.value: FIG. 51. Tetranychus telarius segmentation of the egg. Segmentation consists in the division of the germinal vesicle in the interior, or at the surface of the ovum into two, four, etc. nuclei. These nuclei are each of them surrounded by a specially concentrated layer of protoplasm  which is continuous with a general protoplasmic reticulum passing through the ovum [not shown in fig. 51]. The yolk is contained in the meshes of this reticulum. The ovum, like that of Eupagurus before segmentation, is now a syncytium.
